text:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated p95 latency on /v1/generate (hosted-us-east-1). Current p95=1.2s, p50=120ms. Alert firing: api-high-latency-p95.

Priya S: taking primary. I'm oncall for the evening shift — looking

Carlos M: on standby as secondary. ping me if you need capacity changes or failover.

Priya S: quick customer-impact summary — internal metric shows ~3% error-rate bump and latency spikes for long prompts >1024 tokens. No full outage, customers may see slower responses.

Nina T: adding runbook pointer: https://runbooks.internal.redwood/latency-investigation (see section "KV cache pressure + batching") :eyes:

Priya S: first quick checks — rolling p95 by model instance. Running query now:
```bash
redwood metrics query "p95(api.response_time) by instance" --last 15m --region us-east-1
```

incident-bot: automation: created bridge #latency-bridge-2256789012 and attached traces (trace-id: 0a1b2c).

Priya S: initial findings — one worker group (g4dn-8x) shows high per-token latency and increased GC cycles. suspect kernel/driver bump in that pool.

Carlos M: if it's a single pool, we can route traffic away from that pool temporarily. I can scale down that worker group and bring up warm instances in dedicated capacity pool. Recommend temporary routing policy change.

Priya S: agree. For immediate pager noise reduction I propose a temporary alert cooldown: bump api-high-latency-p95 alert threshold from 500ms to 800ms for 2 hours and add suppression for secondary oncall if error-rate <0.5%. This keeps SLAs intact but reduces duplicate pagers while we mitigate. Thoughts?

Liam R: thumbs up from infra. We also need to document this in the incident timeline.

CS-Triage: we'll prepare a proactive note to impacted customers (small cohort) but won't broadcast system-wide yet. Can you tag affected customer IDs?

Priya S: will export session IDs and sample request ids and drop them in #support-ops. Small cohort = ~12 customers, mostly long-prompt use.

ops-runbooks: runbook step to change alert rule (only eng-sre can apply):
```yaml
- name: temp-bump-latency-alert
  action: update-alert
  alert: api-high-latency-p95
  new_threshold_ms: 800
  duration_min: 120
```
Please run `infractl alerts update --id api-high-latency-p95 --threshold 800 --until now+120m` and post the command output.

Carlos M: executing, posts console output: `OK: alert api-high-latency-p95 threshold set to 800ms until 2026-03-15T04:15:12Z`

Priya S: routing change in progress — shifting 35% of traffic off g4dn-8x to g5 pools and Dedicated overflow. Watch p95 in 5m.

incident-bot: Change applied: routing rule updated (rule-id r-944).

Priya S: p95 on problematic pool dropped to 420ms within 4m. System p95 now 430ms. Noise reduced.

Nina T: good. Can we keep the temp alert bump for exactly 2 hours and schedule an automatic rollback?

Priya S: yes — infractl sets expiry. I'll add note to timeline and schedule rollback at expiry. Also tagging handoff: I'm primary until 04:00 UTC, Carlos is secondary. Nina will pick up next early shift if still active.

CS-Triage: thanks — we drafted the customer note and will hold until you confirm stable for 30m.

Priya S: will update in 30m with stability check. If anything changes, we'll open a follow-up thread. For now: mitigation applied, temporary alert bump in place (800ms, 2h), traffic routing adjusted, CS notified draft ready.

Carlos M: leaving a small follow-up runbook entry for permanent retro: look at kernel/drivers on g4dn pool and also consider autoscaling warm capacity for long prompts.

Priya S: tagged for postmortem. closing bridge after 60m of stable metrics. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Note: alert cooldown applied by Carlos M; rollback scheduled at 2256792612.
